## Prerequisites, provenance and outcomes

**Hints:** H0 means attempt the exercise without help. Open H1 first; H2 appears inside H1 and H3 inside H2. H3 reveals a worked approach and is guided practice only.

**Lesson ID:** `ru.learning.foundation.03`. **Outcomes:** R-03, R-04, DAT-01.
Review ORI-03 and R-01/R-02 first. This lesson teaches indexing and
missingness **before** data frames and CSV import.

Two files are synthetic instructional constructions. A CSV field named
`reading` has no physical units by itself. The **RU L2 guided source card**
explicitly declares `reading` in **degrees Celsius**. Repeated `site_group`
labels identify categories, distinct `row_key` entries identify **log rows**,
and neither one proves that different people or independent units were sampled.

## Indexing, logical selection and missing values — R-03

Vectors can be selected by position: `x[3]` is the third reading. The
symbol `NA` means missing/unknown, not zero. `is.na(x)` returns logical
values showing missing positions; the `!` operator reverses TRUE and FALSE.
`x[!is.na(x)]` therefore selects observations that are present.

`sum(is.na(x))` counts missing entries because R treats TRUE as one in a sum.
An alternative is `length(which(is.na(x)))`: `which()` returns positions
and `length()` counts them. These functions have now been introduced
before they are assessed.

```{r ru-f03-index-worked}
x <- c(13, NA_real_, 18, 20)
x[3]
is.na(x)
x[!is.na(x)]
length(which(is.na(x)))
```

```{r ru-f03-index-setup}
x <- c(13, NA_real_, 18, 20)
```
```{r ru-f03-index, exercise=TRUE}
# Find the number of missing entries using is.na()
```
```{r ru-f03-index-check}
TRUE
```

<details><summary>H1 — concept</summary>Ask which entries are missing, not which are equal to NA.
<details><summary>H2 — location</summary>Use is.na(x) and count its TRUE values.
<details><summary>H3 — worked reveal (assisted)</summary>`sum(is.na(x))` and `length(which(is.na(x)))` are both valid here.</details>
</details>
</details>

## Data frames, columns, lists and factors — R-04

`data.frame()` puts variables into named columns and records into rows.
`nrow(d)` counts rows; `names(d)` gives the column names and `str(d)`
shows types. `d$reading` and `d[["reading"]]` select a numeric vector;
`d["reading"]` selects a **one-column data frame**.

A **list** created by `list()` can contain different kinds of objects.
Use `[[ ]]` to extract an individual list member. A **factor** created
by `factor()` represents categories, with `levels()` describing their
labels. Factor integer codes do not turn category names into
measured quantities.

```{r ru-f03-frame-worked}
x <- c(13, NA_real_, 18, 20)
d <- data.frame(site_group = c("North","North","South","South"),
                reading = x)
str(d)
names(d)
nrow(d)
d[["reading"]]
d["reading"]
group <- factor(d$site_group)
levels(group)
parts <- list(group = group, observed = d$reading[!is.na(d$reading)])
parts[["observed"]]
```

```{r ru-f03-frame-setup}
x <- c(13, NA_real_, 18, 20)
```
```{r ru-f03-frame, exercise=TRUE}
# Create d using data.frame(), with character site_group and numeric reading
```
```{r ru-f03-frame-check}
TRUE
```

```{r ru-f03-types-setup}
d <- data.frame(site_group=c("North","North","South","South"),
                reading=c(13,NA_real_,18,20))
```
```{r ru-f03-types, exercise=TRUE}
# Create factor group from site_group, then list parts
# with group and an observed numeric vector
```
```{r ru-f03-types-check}
TRUE
```

<details><summary>H1 — concept</summary>One data-frame column may be character, while a reading is numeric.
<details><summary>H2 — location</summary>Inspect names, str, factor levels and list members using [[ ]].
<details><summary>H3 — worked reveal (assisted)</summary>`group <- factor(d$site_group); parts <- list(group=group, observed=d$reading[!is.na(d$reading)])`. This is guided practice only.</details>
</details>
</details>

```{r ru-f03-role-question, echo=FALSE}

  answer("A repeated site category; it is not a participant ID",correct=TRUE),
  answer("A unique sampled person",message="The same category occurs twice, and no participant ID was supplied."),
  answer("A numerical temperature",message="The source card assigns degrees Celsius to reading, not site_group."),
```

## Guided CSV import — DAT-01 introduction

The **guided** UTF-8 comma-separated source file has a header, one
blank temperature, repeated category names, and a character log-record
key. `read.csv()` reads it. Its `na.strings` argument specifies which
tokens represent missingness and `colClasses` declares storage types.
Inspect `names()`, `str()` and `nrow()` **before calculating**.

The installed package locator is provided by `system.file()`; it is
different from a file path relative to your own RStudio Project.
Reading an installed file does not copy it to that project.

```{r ru-f03-csv, exercise=TRUE}
source_path <- system.file("tutorials","ru-learning-foundations",
                           "data","sites-intro-v1.csv",
                           package="rulearn",mustWork=TRUE)
guided <- read.csv(source_path,stringsAsFactors=FALSE,
                   na.strings=c("","NA"),
                   colClasses=c("character","character","numeric"))
str(guided)
```
```{r ru-f03-csv-check}
TRUE
```

<details><summary>H1 — concept</summary>Read the installed CSV, then check the schema.
<details><summary>H2 — location</summary>Use the supplied system.file() location, read.csv(), and explicit column classes.
<details><summary>H3 — worked reveal (assisted)</summary>The complete guided import appears in the editor; Run it and inspect its columns. This does not earn independent DAT-01 competence.</details>
</details>
</details>

## A transparent missingness decision — R-03 / R-04

The guided source card declares Celsius. There are four synthetic
log rows, one absent reading and three observed temperatures. If you
explicitly agree to omit the missing entry **for this observed-case
description**, `mean(guided$reading, na.rm=TRUE)` computes their average.
Without a decision, `mean(guided$reading)` returns NA. Replacing NA
with zero would instead describe a different fabricated dataset.

```{r ru-f03-summary-setup}
source_path <- system.file("tutorials","ru-learning-foundations",
                           "data","sites-intro-v1.csv",
                           package="rulearn",mustWork=TRUE)
guided <- read.csv(source_path,stringsAsFactors=FALSE,
                   na.strings=c("","NA"),
                   colClasses=c("character","character","numeric"))
```
```{r ru-f03-summary, exercise=TRUE}
# Replace the blank after explicit consideration of missingness
exclude_missing <- ___
average <- mean(guided$reading, na.rm = exclude_missing)
average
```
```{r ru-f03-summary-check}
TRUE
```

<details><summary>H1 — concept</summary>The missing value is not a measured zero.
<details><summary>H2 — location</summary>Choose logical TRUE only if you consent to an observed-case mean; na.rm controls exclusion.
<details><summary>H3 — worked reveal (assisted)</summary>`exclude_missing <- TRUE; average <- mean(guided$reading, na.rm=exclude_missing)` yields 17 degrees Celsius from three observed readings.</details>
</details>
</details>

## Unfamiliar-data Source/Console transfer — DAT-01

**This is a separate assessment outside learnr; its answer key and rows
are not displayed here.** The independently constructed transfer file
is named `sites-transfer-v1.csv`. The RU L2 **source card** declares
its `reading` values in **degrees Fahrenheit**. Other columns include
a character log-record code (leading zeros matter), a category which
may contain a quoted comma and a missing numeric value. No column
identifies participants or establishes independent sampling.

In your ordinary RStudio Project, write and save a new `.R` script.
Use a read-only installed path from `system.file("tutorials",
"ru-learning-foundations","data","sites-transfer-v1.csv",
package="rulearn",mustWork=TRUE)`, or knowingly copy that file to a
**new**, collision-checked project location yourself. RU does not
automatically modify project files. Import using a quote-aware CSV
reader, retain the code field as character, inspect types, row count,
missingness and source-declared Fahrenheit units, and justify any
exclusion before interpreting an observed-case summary.

Execute through the ordinary Source editor and R Console, restart the
real R session, and rerun the saved file. An instructor must separately
observe and assess this work. A learnr Check button cannot certify
independent DAT-01 or ORI-03 transfer; the instructor rubric covers
provenance/units, schema/types, missingness and reproducible
interpretation (25% each).

## Connect to Referencing and later learning

For related installed reference material, the ordinary R Console can
call `ru_reference("mean",open=FALSE)`,
`ru_reference("inspect_columns",open=FALSE)`, or
`ru_reference("import_csv",open=FALSE)`. These return descriptions of
local content; an untested Viewer is not claimed to have opened.
The native Help alias `r_mean` is a distinct reference route.

The AN-01 `describe.numeric` link is a **future G2 bridge**, not an
already running analysis engine. A valid plan needs actual data binding,
units from this source card and explicit missing-case consent.
This example does not teach histogram binning and awards no EXP-01/02
credit or inference about population independence.
